name: Research papers
description: Papers, authors, affiliations, venues, datasets, methods, tasks, metrics, results, citations and funding.
purpose: Turn a collection of scholarly articles into a graph of who did what, on which data, with which results, so literature reviews and benchmark comparisons can be answered by query instead of re-reading.
scope: In scope: bibliographic metadata, authors and affiliations, venues, datasets, methods, tasks, evaluation metrics, reported results, citations between papers, and grants. Out of scope: full-text argument mining, peer-review data and citation-count analytics.
stories: As a researcher I want every reported result linked to its method, dataset, task and metric so that I can build a leaderboard across papers.
As a literature reviewer I want papers linked to the methods they propose and the datasets they use so that I can map the state of the art for a task.
As a research-office manager I want papers linked to grants, funders and author affiliations so that I can report outputs per funding award and institution.
cqs: Which authors wrote a given paper, and with which institutions are they affiliated?
In which venue and year was each paper published, and what is its DOI?
Which papers address a given task, and which methods do they propose?
Which datasets does each paper use?
What is the best reported score for a given task, dataset and metric, and which method achieved it?
Which results in a paper are baselines and which belong to the proposed method?
Which papers cite a given paper?
Which grants, and which funding agencies, supported a given paper?
Which papers come from authors at institutions in a given country?
